title: Synonyms and Antonyms
tagline: Year 1 Foundation — Words with the same and opposite meanings, and how to choose between them

introduction.overview: A synonym is a word with the same or nearly the same meaning as another word (begin and start). An antonym is a word with the opposite meaning (strong and weak). Placement tests ask for the closest synonym or antonym of a given word, often with options that include a confusing near-miss. Success depends on knowing the core meaning of the word, whether it is positive or negative in tone, and which part of speech it is.
introduction.placementRelevance: Synonym and antonym questions are commonly asked in the verbal ability section of company aptitude rounds. They are quick, so accuracy and a steady vocabulary routine pay off directly.
introduction.realWorldContext: Writers use synonyms to avoid repeating the same word and to find a more precise one. Antonyms help to contrast ideas clearly in reports and emails.

learningObjectives: Identify the closest synonym and the exact antonym of a word
Recognise shades of meaning and tone (positive, negative, neutral)
Use prefixes to form antonyms and to spot trap options
Eliminate options that are related but not opposite
Build a routine for pairing every new word with a synonym and an antonym

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: The class of the word matters: a synonym of a verb is a verb, and a synonym of an adjective is an adjective. The tone matters too: stubborn (negative) is not the same as determined (positive), although both describe someone who does not change their mind.

coreDefinitions: Synonym: a word that has the same or nearly the same meaning as another word in a given context.
Antonym: a word that has the opposite meaning. Types include gradable (hot/cold), complementary (alive/dead) and relational (buy/sell).
Connotation: the feeling a word carries beyond its dictionary meaning (positive, negative or neutral).
Near-miss option: a distractor that is related in meaning but not a true synonym or antonym.
Context: the sentence in which the word appears, which often decides the correct meaning of a word with more than one sense.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The correct option is the one you could substitute into the sentence without changing its meaning (synonym) or whose meaning reverses the original (antonym). Be careful with words that have several meanings: "fair" can mean just, light-coloured or fairly good, and the context tells you which one is meant.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: For a synonym, put the answer in place of the word in a short sentence and check that it reads naturally. For an antonym, check that the answer really is the opposite and not merely different. "Cold" is the antonym of "hot", but "wet" is not.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Substitution test (synonym)
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Replace the word with the option in a sentence
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: The meaning must stay the same.
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: The soldier was brave → courageous works

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Opposite test (antonym)
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: The option must reverse the meaning
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Check that it is not merely different.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Tone check
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Positive ↔ positive in synonyms; positive ↔ negative in antonyms

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Prefix antonyms
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: un-, in-, im-, dis-, non- build many antonyms
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Not every antonym uses a prefix.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Common word pairs
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: conceal = hide; tranquil = calm; candid = frank; mitigate = lessen; expand ↔ contract; scarce ↔ plentiful; transparent ↔ opaque; zenith ↔ nadir
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Revise a few new pairs every day.

mainNarrative: For a synonym, find the option whose meaning matches the word most closely in the usual sense. The word courageous means brave. An option such as "foolish" is not a synonym even though foolish people may take risks. Always avoid options that are only loosely connected.

For an antonym, find the true opposite. The antonym of generous is stingy (unwilling to give). The option "rich" is not an antonym; a rich person can be generous or stingy. Remember that antonyms are about meaning, not about spelling or prefixes.

Many questions give one correct answer and one or two near-misses. "Candid" means frank and honest. "Polite" and "secretive" are traps: polite is different in meaning, and secretive is nearly opposite. Check the tone and the main sense before choosing.

Words with several meanings change their synonyms with context. In "a fair judge", fair means just; in "a fair complexion", it means light. If the question gives no sentence, choose the most common meaning.

To build vocabulary quickly, write each new word with one synonym, one antonym and a sentence. Revise the same words after one day, one week and one month. This spaced revision is more effective than reading a long list once.

deepDiveAspects.title: Degrees of meaning
deepDiveAspects.content: Synonyms are rarely identical. Small, tiny and minute all relate to size but at different degrees; huge, enormous and gigantic are all very large. In tests, choose the option closest in degree to the given word.

deepDiveAspects.title: Antonyms with prefixes versus without
deepDiveAspects.content: Some antonyms are formed with prefixes (possible → impossible), while others are separate words (permanent ↔ temporary). Do not assume that every antonym takes a prefix. Check whether the prefixed word is meaningful and commonly used.

problemVariations.exampleSnippet: Antonym of "fair" in a fair complexion.

solvedExamples.title: Synonym with a near-miss
solvedExamples.question: Choose the synonym of "obstinate": (flexible / stubborn / gentle / wise)
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Match the core meaning and the tone.

steps.title: Find the core meaning
steps.explanation: Obstinate means unwilling to change one's opinion or behaviour, despite good reasons.

steps.title: Compare the options
steps.explanation: Stubborn has the same meaning and tone. Flexible is the opposite; gentle and wise are unrelated.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The substitution test works: "an obstinate child" = "a stubborn child".
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Choosing "wise" because both are about personality.

solvedExamples.title: Antonym that is not simply "different"
solvedExamples.question: Choose the antonym of "generous": (rich / stingy / kind / poor)

steps.title: Find the meaning
steps.explanation: Generous means willing to give freely.

steps.title: Reverse it
steps.explanation: The opposite is unwilling to give, which is stingy.

steps.title: Reject the traps
steps.explanation: Rich and poor describe wealth, not giving; kind is a synonym.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: A person who is poor can still be generous; the relationship is about giving, not money.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Choosing "poor" because it looks opposite to "rich".

solvedExamples.title: Antonym without a prefix
solvedExamples.question: Choose the antonym of "permanent": (temporary / impermanent / fixed / lasting)
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Prefixes do not always create the opposite word used in tests.

steps.title: Find the meaning
steps.explanation: Permanent means lasting for a long time or forever.

steps.title: Find the opposite
steps.explanation: Temporary means lasting only for a short time.

steps.title: Check the other options
steps.explanation: Fixed and lasting are close to permanent.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Temporary is the standard antonym of permanent.

shortcutMethods.title: Substitute and reverse

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Compare every option with every meaning of the word.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Say the word in a simple sentence. Test each option by replacing it (synonym) or by checking that it flips the meaning (antonym). Cross out options that are merely related.

rulesForApplication: Match the part of speech and the tone.
If two options are synonyms of each other, neither is likely to be the answer to an antonym question.
Prefix-formed words are not always the intended antonym.
If the word has several meanings, choose the one in the sentence or the commonest one.

commonMistakes.mistake: Choosing a related word instead of a synonym

commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Check that the option reverses the same quality.
Match or reverse the tone as required.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming a prefix always makes the antonym

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Remove options that are synonyms of each other; one of the remaining may be the answer to an antonym question.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Do these questions quickly. If you do not know the word, use the prefix, root and tone to eliminate options.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: A little daily reading and a notebook of new words gives better results than any last-minute list.

summaryBullets: Synonym = same meaning; antonym = opposite meaning.
Check the part of speech and the tone.
Substitution test for synonyms; reversal test for antonyms.
Learn new words in pairs with a sentence.

keyTakeaways: Opposite is not the same as different.
Context settles words with many meanings.
selfCheckQuestions: Can I give a synonym and an antonym of "generous"?
Can I spot a near-miss option?
Can I explain why "temporary" is the antonym of "permanent"?
